- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are rising steadily, reduce forecast slope if true outcome shows early mean reversion or downward correction.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect — cap forecast growth to 2–3% per period to avoid overshoot.
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is bearish, model overestimates upside — apply downward bias of 1–2% per event horizon.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often fails to adjust mid-cycle — use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day trend, not 30-day trend.
- If recent events are auction-driven and supply net is negative, forecast should not exceed 10% above recent 14-day high — avoid overconfidence in bullish sentiment.
